Hi Laura — thanks for the clear info and the verification attachment. Acknowledged; we can assist. Quick summary of next steps I propose (to get alignment before we start exports/deletions):

1) Scope confirmation (you): please confirm whether the request is only for primary account 4f1a or if linked subaccounts should be included.
2) Export format (we can do JSON or CSV): you requested JSON; we will include personal data fields + last_login, associated tokens/keys (if applicable) as redacted or hashed per DPA rules, and a separate access-log CSV with IP timestamps.
3) Identity verification: we will rely on the signed verification you attached, but we need one additional confirmatory header from an Acme security contact (quick email from acme-privacy) for our audit trail.
4) Delivery: secure, time-limited S3 link with AES-256 server-side encryption and optional PGP envelope if you want an additional layer. Please confirm preference.
5) SLA & timeline: we can target initial export package within 10 business days of confirmation and verification, and a deletion confirmation package within 30 calendar days of export (subject to backup retention windows; see note below).
6) Controller/processor roles: tagging Priya on the formal statement and Rishi on technical export.

Notes on backups/replica: physical deletion from active DBs is straightforward; immutable backups and geo-replicas may require longer retention cycles and selective suppression — we'll include the remediation plan and expected retention windows in the deletion confirmation.

I attached a lightweight checklist we use (redwood_data_export_checklist.csv) so you can confirm fields you need. If that looks good, we'll kick off verification and the technical export.

Hi Laura and team — copied legal/compliance here for clarity. Short legal note to avoid downstream confusion:

- For Hosted API and Dedicated (Redwood-managed) deployments where AcmeCorp sends customer data to Redwood’s platform, Redwood acts as a processor and AcmeCorp is the controller. Our role is to process on your documented instructions in the DPA.
- For Private/on-prem installs where Redwood software is deployed in customer-controlled environments, the customer typically acts as both controller and processor for their own environment — Redwood has no access to customer data in those cases unless explicitly granted.

Attached is our formal statement (controller_processor_statement.pdf) that outlines obligations and references the SCC addendum we have in our DPA. Per contract, we will:
- Provide the export described above in the agreed format
- Perform deletions on our systems and provide a signed deletion confirmation with an audit id
- Document backup retention exceptions and a remediation schedule if deletion from backups requires a retention window

Operationally, to proceed we need:
1) Confirmation of exact user scope (reply to this thread)
2) Preferred transfer method (S3 link vs PGP)
3) An acme-privacy confirmation email for identity verification (simple one-line reply is fine)

Happy to hop on a short call if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
